newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Air Jamaica, BWIA to share services.
newsitem.headline: Air Jamaica, BWIA to share services.

text.p: Air Jamaica and Trinidad's British West Indies Airways (BWIA) said Tuesday they had formed a partnership that would cut costs and pave the way for a long-term alliance.
Air Jamaica Chairman Gordon "Butch" Stewart said cost cutting was crucial as his airline has lost more than US$100 million since it was privatized two and a half years ago.
He blamed the losses on Jamaica's failure to get a Category I rating from the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration, which forced Air Jamaica into expensive lease agreements to service U.S. routes.

Stewart said that, as of June 30, Air Jamaica and BWIA will have joint fuel purchasing and catering arrangements, joint check-in and ramp services at the Miami and Kingston airports and common space and ground handling in New York.
The alliance's long-term goals include code sharing and cross-utilization of aircraft and the companies hoped to have more information on how to pursue those options by the end of the year.
